explanation: For d ≥ 2, AME(7,d) exists iff d ≥ 3. AME(7,2) fails by Huber–Gühne–Siewert. The d ≥ 3 direction relies on Shi–Zhang–Zhao–Li (2026, arXiv:2608.01011), which claims a complete classification, together with the known prime-power constructions. Excluding d = 1, where the trivial state is AME under this definition, is handled correctly. The statement is consistent with the cited source. I did not independently verify the 2026 preprint.
